title: A Stranger in the Promised Land

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Abraham rose from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hittites. He said, "I am a foreigner and stranger among you. Sell me some property for a burial site here so I can bury my dead." - Gen 23:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham rises from his grief to attend to a practical need - a place to bury Sarah. And listen to how he describes himself: "I am a foreigner and stranger among you." After decades of living in Canaan, the land God had promised him, Abraham still owned not one square foot of it. He remained a resident alien, a stranger in the very land pledged to his descendants.

There is something profound here. God had promised Abraham this whole land, yet throughout his life he held that promise by faith, not by possession. He lived as a pilgrim, trusting God's word about a future he would not fully see. His faith rested not on what he could grasp in his hand, but on what God had spoken.

The New Testament reflects on exactly this. Abraham and the other patriarchs "were foreigners and strangers on earth," people who lived "longing for a better country - a heavenly one" (Heb 11:13, 16). Their true home was not finally this land at all, but the eternal city God was preparing.

And this is our calling too. Believers are "foreigners and exiles" in this world (1 Pet 2:11), citizens of heaven passing through. We hold the things of this life loosely, because our lasting home is elsewhere. Like Abraham, we may not possess much here, but we have God's promise of an eternal inheritance. Live as a pilgrim today, with your heart set on the better country God has prepared for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you live as a pilgrim, holding this world loosely?
- Is your heart set on the eternal home God has prepared?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, like Abraham I am a stranger passing through this world. Help me hold its things loosely and set my heart on the better country You have prepared. Thank You for my eternal inheritance in Christ.
Amen.
